texts.li: Since the digging, stone lies everywhere inside the colony's bounds: heaped by the doors, scattered across the yard, in the way of every barrow. {A_nameDef} wants it brought in, or cut into blocks for the walls. {B_nameDef} says the fields need every hand this week, and the stone isn't going anywhere.

{A_nameDef} tripped over the same lump of rock on the way to the council and took it as a sign. The yard is full of stone from the digging, {A_pronoun} says, and every piece of it could be a wall. {B_nameDef} says it could also wait.

[lowtech] The stones from the digging lie all about the huts, and the children have built a fort of them by the fire pit. {A_nameDef} wants them brought to the heap and shaped for the walls. {B_nameDef} says the fields come first, as they always have.

[!lowtech] Rubble from the digging lies all over the colony's ground, and {A_nameDef} has been saying for days that it is good stone wasted. {B_nameDef} says the crops won't wait while the colony tidies its yard.

li.label: Everyone carries the stone in
li.outcome: A few of the colony are to carry the stone in from the yard and the doorways for a few hours, one load at a time.

lines.li: Mind your back with that one.
Two more loads and we stop for water.
Who left this one in the doorway?

li.label: Cut it into blocks at the stonecutter's
li.outcome: A bill for blocks is set at the stonecutter's bench, first in line, for the stone that lies about.

li.label: The fields first
li.outcome: The council said the fields come first. The stone stays where it lies.

li.label: the stone brought in
li.description: The council had the stone brought in from the yard. I can walk to my own door without climbing over rocks.

li.label: the fields left waiting
li.description: Half the colony is moving stone while the fields go untended. I said it could wait.

li.label: good stone put to use
li.description: The stone from the digging is to be cut into blocks. It will be a wall one day instead of something to trip over.

li.label: the stone left lying
li.description: The council left the stone where it lies. I'll be stepping round it for weeks.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has never been any good in the mornings, and it is getting worse. {A_pronoun} works half asleep all day and lies awake all night. {A_pronoun} asks the council to let {A_objective} keep the night hours, when {A_pronoun} is at {A_possessive} best. {B_nameDef} says the colony works by day, all of it, and that's that.

[roommate] {A_nameDef} wants to work through the nights and sleep by day. {B_nameDef}, who shares {A_possessive} room, says that means someone coming in at dawn and the curtains drawn at noon, and isn't keen.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} sits up by the fire every night long after the others have gone to sleep, and is no use to anyone in the morning. {A_pronoun} would rather work while the others sleep, and sleep while they work. {B_nameDef} says the day is for work and the night is for sleep.

li.label: {A_nameDef} keeps the night hours for a while
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is to work the nights and sleep through the days for a while, and come back to the colony's hours after.

li.label: One night at the bench, to see how it goes
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is to work through tonight and sleep the morning after, to see how it goes.

li.label: The colony keeps one day
li.outcome: The council said the colony keeps one day for all of it. {A_nameDef} will have to get used to the mornings.

li.label: my own hours
li.description: The council let me keep the night hours. I work when I'm awake and sleep when I'm tired, and I feel like myself again.

li.label: someone up all night
li.description: The council let one of us keep the night hours. It's strange having someone up and about while the rest of us sleep.

li.label: a night at the work
li.description: The council let me try a night at the work. It was the best I've worked in weeks.

li.label: mornings again
li.description: The council said I keep the same hours as everyone else. I'm awake when I should be asleep and asleep when I should be awake.

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.label: the seat while its holder is away

texts.li: {A_nameDef}, the {OFFICE}, is away from the colony, and the seat's work has waited for {A_objective} ever since {A_pronoun} left. {B_nameDef} knows enough of it to keep it going, and has offered, if the council agrees.

[caravan] {A_nameDef} is out on the road with the caravan, and nobody is doing the {OFFICE}'s work while {A_pronoun} is gone. {B_nameDef} has asked the council whether {B_pronoun} should take it on until {A_nameDef} is home.
[far] {A_nameDef}, the {OFFICE}, is far from home, and the things that are the {OFFICE}'s to see to are piling up. {B_nameDef} says someone ought to see to them, and is willing.

[lowtech] The {OFFICE} is away, and the matters that are {A_nameDef}'s to settle are piling up by the door of the long hut. {B_nameDef} has offered to settle them until {A_nameDef} is back by the fire.

li.label: {B_nameDef} stands in for {A_nameDef} for a while
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} takes on the {OFFICE}'s work for a while, in {A_nameDef}'s place.

li.label: {B_nameDef} reads out the seat's business at supper
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} will read out what is waiting for the {OFFICE} at supper, so the colony knows how things stand until {A_nameDef} is home.

lines.li: Here is what is waiting for the {OFFICE}, so nobody can say they didn't know.
None of this is mine to settle, but all of it should be heard.
{A_nameDef} will have plenty to see to when {A_pronoun} gets home.

li.label: The seat waits for {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: The council said the seat is {A_nameDef}'s, and its work waits until {A_pronoun} is home.

li.label: trusted with a seat's work
li.description: The council asked me to do the work of a seat while its holder is away. They trust me with it.

li.label: the seat's business read out
li.description: I read out the seat's business at supper so everyone knows where things stand. It's the least anyone could do.

li.label: my seat kept for me
li.description: I heard the council kept my seat's work for me while I was away. Nobody tried to take it over.

li.label: my offer turned down
li.description: I offered to do the seat's work while its holder is away, and the council said it can wait. So it waits.

texts.li: {DECREE} has the whole colony working harder, and it is more than {A_nameDef} can manage. {A_pronoun} has asked the council for some ease while it lasts. {B_nameDef} could take on {A_possessive} {WORK}, if the council says so.

[elder] {DECREE} is hard on everyone, and harder on {A_nameDef}, who is not as young as the rest of them. {A_pronoun} has asked the council for some ease while it lasts. {B_nameDef} could take on {A_possessive} {WORK} until it is over.
[ill] {A_nameDef} is unwell, and {DECREE} gives {A_objective} no room to get better. {A_pronoun} asks the council for ease while it lasts. {B_nameDef} could do {A_possessive} {WORK} in the meantime.
[injured] {A_nameDef}'s old injury has been bad since {DECREE} began, and {A_pronoun} came to the council favouring it. {B_nameDef} could take on {A_possessive} {WORK} while the decree lasts.
[worn] {A_nameDef} is worn to the bone with {DECREE}, and says so. {B_nameDef} could take on {A_possessive} {WORK} until the decree ends, if the council asks it.

[lowtech] Since the council's word went out for {DECREE}, {A_nameDef} has dragged {A_objective}self from the fire to the work and back, and has asked for ease. {B_nameDef} could do {A_possessive} {WORK} for a while.

li.label: {A_nameDef} has today off
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has today off, decree or not.

li.label: {B_nameDef} takes on {A_nameDef}'s {WORK} while the decree lasts
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} does {A_nameDef}'s {WORK} until {DECREE} ends, and then it goes back to {A_objective}.

li.label: The decree is for the whole colony
li.outcome: The council said the decree is for the whole colony, and that includes {A_nameDef}.

li.label: a day off from the decree
li.description: The council gave me a day off in the middle of the decree. I needed it more than I let on.

li.label: my work lightened
li.description: Someone else is doing my work while the decree lasts. I can get through it now.

li.label: someone else's work too
li.description: I'm doing my own work and someone else's while the decree lasts. Someone has to, I suppose.

li.label: no ease from the decree
li.description: I asked the council for some ease while the decree lasts, and they said it's for everyone. I know that. It's still too much for me.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is the finest hand at {SKILL} anyone here has seen, and {A_nameDef} has followed {X_objective} about the colony since {X_pronoun} arrived. {A_pronoun} wants the council to ask {X_nameDef} for an afternoon of teaching. {B_nameDef} says the visitors are here to trade, not to be pestered.

{A_nameDef} watched {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} for an hour this morning and came to the council bright-eyed. Nobody at the colony is half as good at {SKILL}, {A_pronoun} says, and here {X_pronoun} is. {B_nameDef} thinks a guest should be let alone.

[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef}, who came with the {FACTION} visitors, works at {SKILL} in a way {A_nameDef} has never seen, and {A_nameDef} can talk about nothing else. {B_nameDef} thinks a guest should be left in peace by the fire.

[seat] {HOLDER_nameDef}, the {OFFICE}, says {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} would likely teach a little {SKILL} if asked. {A_nameDef} is ready to drop everything for it. {B_nameDef} says the colony shouldn't make work for its guests.

li.label: An afternoon at {X_nameDef}'s side
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} agreed to show {A_nameDef} how {X_pronoun} works, and {A_nameDef} will spend the afternoon at {X_possessive} side.

li.label: {A_nameDef} sits with {X_nameDef} at supper and asks about it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} will sit across from {X_nameDef} at supper and ask {X_objective} everything {A_pronoun} can think of.

li.label: Guests are left to their business
li.outcome: The council said guests are left to their business. {A_nameDef} looked on from a distance and said nothing.

li.label: learned from a master
li.description: A visitor who really knows the craft let me work beside them. I learned more in an afternoon than in a season on my own.

li.label: talked the craft with a master
li.description: I sat with a visitor who knows the craft far better than I do and asked every question I had. They answered all of them.

li.label: a chance missed
li.description: The best at my craft I've ever met was right here, and the council wouldn't let me ask them anything.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, in the colony's cell, is shaking with cold, and the cell is hardly warmer than the yard. {A_nameDef}, who keeps the cell, wants something done about it. {B_nameDef} says a prisoner who is cold is a prisoner who thinks twice about raiding again.

{A_nameDef} came back from the cell with frost on {A_possessive} sleeves and asked for a fire for {X_nameDef}, who can't stop shivering. {B_nameDef} would rather the wood went to the colony's own rooms.

[lowtech] The cold has got into the cell hut, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} lies curled up against the wall. {A_nameDef} asks for a fire in there. {B_nameDef} says the colony's fires are for the colony.
[seat] {HOLDER_nameDef}, the {OFFICE}, says the cell is too cold for anyone to sleep in. {A_nameDef} wants a fire lit in there for {X_nameDef}; {B_nameDef} doesn't see why.

li.label: A fire in the cell
li.outcome: A fire is set in a corner of {X_nameDef}'s cell, with wood enough for a few nights.

li.label: {A_nameDef} takes {X_nameDef} a hot meal
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} takes a hot meal from the stores in to {X_nameDef}, who eats it there in the cell.

li.label: The cell stays as it is
li.outcome: The council said the cell stays as it is.

li.label: a fire in my cell
li.description: They lit a fire in my cell. I'm still a prisoner, but at least I can feel my hands.

li.label: the council listened about the cell
li.description: I asked for a fire in the cell and the council agreed. Nobody should freeze in our keeping.

li.label: our wood for a prisoner
li.description: Our wood is going to keep a prisoner warm. I can think of better uses for it.

li.label: a hot meal in the cold
li.description: Someone brought me a hot meal in the cell. It's the first warm thing I've had in days.

li.label: the cold cell
li.description: I keep the cell, and the council won't let me do anything about the cold in it. I don't like what that says about us.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has worked every day since {X_pronoun} was brought here, and it shows: {X_pronoun} moves like someone twice {X_possessive} age and hardly speaks. {A_nameDef} asks the council to give {X_objective} some rest. {B_nameDef} says the slaves are kept to their work, and rest only makes them bold.

{A_nameDef} has been watching {X_nameDef} at the work, and doesn't like what {A_pronoun} sees. {A_pronoun} wants {X_nameDef} given the rest of the day. {B_nameDef} says it would only be the first of many.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, the colony's thrall, fell asleep standing at the work this morning. {A_nameDef} asks that {X_pronoun} be let off for the rest of the day. {B_nameDef} says the work doesn't stop because a thrall is tired.
[seat] {HOLDER_nameDef}, the {OFFICE}, has said nothing either way, so {A_nameDef} has brought it to the council: {X_nameDef} is worn out and needs rest. {B_nameDef} says no.

li.label: {X_nameDef} rests the rest of today
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is let off the work for the rest of today.

li.label: {A_nameDef} speaks for {X_nameDef} at supper
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} will say a few words for {X_nameDef} at supper, so the colony hears how hard {X_pronoun} works.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} works as hard as any of us, and the colony should know it.
Nobody here has carried more than {X_nameDef} this season.

li.label: The work is theirs
li.outcome: The council said the work is {X_possessive}, rest or no rest.

li.label: an afternoon's rest
li.description: They let me stop working for the rest of the day. I sat down and didn't get up for hours.

li.label: soft on the slaves
li.description: The council gave a slave the afternoon off. Next they'll all be asking.

li.label: someone spoke for me
li.description: One of them stood up at supper and said how hard I work. Nobody has ever done that.

li.label: spoke up for someone
li.description: I said at supper how hard one of the slaves works. Somebody had to say it.

li.label: no rest
li.description: Someone asked for me to rest, and the council said no. I'm so tired.

li.label: not heard
li.description: I asked the council for an afternoon's rest for one of the slaves, and they wouldn't hear of it.

texts.li: {PET_nameDef} sleeps out with the other animals, and every morning {PET_pronoun} is waiting at {A_nameDef}'s door. {A_nameDef} wants a {THING} for {PET_objective} in the corner of {A_possessive} room. {B_nameDef}, who sees to the animals, says an animal in a bedroom means hair and mess, and an animal sleeps best with its own kind.

{A_nameDef} has been letting {PET_nameDef} in at night anyway, and the council has heard about it. {A_pronoun} asks for a proper {THING} in {A_possessive} room for {PET_objective}. {B_nameDef} says the barn is where animals sleep.

[lowtech] {PET_nameDef} curls up against the wall of {A_nameDef}'s hut every night, out in the cold. {A_nameDef} asks for a place for {PET_objective} inside, by {A_possessive} bed. {B_nameDef} says the animals have their own shelter and always have.
[seat] {HOLDER_nameDef}, the {OFFICE}, has no objection to {PET_nameDef} sleeping in {A_nameDef}'s room. {B_nameDef} does, and says so.

li.label: A {THING} for {PET_nameDef} in {A_nameDef}'s room
li.outcome: A {THING} is set in a corner of {A_nameDef}'s room for {PET_nameDef}.

li.label: {A_nameDef} sits with {PET_nameDef} of an evening instead
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} will spend this evening with {PET_nameDef} wherever {PET_pronoun} is, and {PET_nameDef} keeps sleeping where the animals sleep.

li.label: Animals sleep where animals sleep
li.outcome: The council said animals sleep where animals sleep.

li.label: my animal by my bed
li.description: My animal has a bed of its own in my room now. I hear it breathing in the dark, and I sleep better for it.

li.label: animals in the bedrooms
li.description: The council put an animal's bed in someone's room. I'll be sweeping up the hair.

li.label: an evening with my animal
li.description: I spent the evening with my animal. It isn't the same as having it by my bed, but it helped.

li.label: my animal kept out
li.description: I asked for my animal to sleep in my room, and the council said no. It waits at my door every morning.

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.label: the dry grass by the walls

texts.li: It has not rained in a long while, and the grass has grown tall and dry right up to the colony's walls. {A_nameDef} pulled a handful and it crumbled in {A_possessive} fingers. One spark, {A_pronoun} says, and the whole edge of the colony would go up. {A_pronoun} wants a strip cut bare all the way round. {B_nameDef} says there is more pressing work than cutting grass.

{A_nameDef} has walked the edge of the colony twice today, looking at the dry brush where it meets the walls. {A_pronoun} wants a firebreak cut before the next lightning. {B_nameDef} would rather the hands went to the building.

[lowtech] The grass grows right up to the huts, brown and dry as tinder. {A_nameDef} remembers a village that burned in a summer like this one, and wants it cut back. {B_nameDef} says there has always been grass by the huts.
[seat] {HOLDER_nameDef}, the {OFFICE}, agrees with {A_nameDef} that the dry grass by the walls is a danger in this heat. {B_nameDef} says the colony has more pressing work.

li.label: Cut a firebreak round the walls
li.outcome: The dry grass and brush at the edge of the colony is marked for cutting, and a few of the colony will cut it back from the walls.

lines.li: Cut it right down, it's no good half done.
Rake it away from the wall, not toward it.

li.label: {A_nameDef} walks the walls at dusk watching for smoke
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} will walk the colony's edge at dusk, looking out for smoke.

li.label: The grass can stay
li.outcome: The council said the grass can stay. {A_nameDef} said what {A_pronoun} thought of that, and went back to work.

li.label: a firebreak cut
li.description: The grass is cut back from the walls. If a fire comes, it has nothing to climb.

li.label: watching for smoke
li.description: I walk the walls at dusk looking for smoke. It's not a firebreak, but I'd see a fire coming.

li.label: the grass by the walls
li.description: The grass stands dry right up to the walls, and the council won't have it cut. I keep looking at the sky.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} holds to {GOD}, and says the colony eats every evening without a word of thanks to anyone. {A_pronoun} would like {GOD}'s words said before supper, at the table, where everyone can hear them. {B_nameDef}, who holds to no god at all, says {B_pronoun} would like to eat {B_possessive} supper while it's hot.
[priest] {A_nameDef}, who leads the colony's worship, asks that {GOD}'s words be said before supper. {B_nameDef} says {B_pronoun} will sit through no such thing, and would rather eat outside.

[lowtech] Before the pot is passed round, {A_nameDef} wants {GOD} thanked, as {A_possessive} people always did. {B_nameDef} says the food was grown and cooked by the colony's own hands, and it is the hands that should be thanked.

li.label: {GOD}'s words before supper tonight
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} will say {GOD}'s words at the table before supper tonight, and the colony will hear them before it eats.

lines.li: Be thou thanked, {GOD}, for what is set before us this night.
We eat by thy leave, {GOD}, and we forget it not.
Bless this bread, {GOD}, and the hands that made it.

li.label: {A_nameDef} says the words at {PLACE}, and the table eats as it likes
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} says {GOD}'s words at {PLACE} before supper, and the table eats as it likes.

li.label: Each keeps their own thanks
li.outcome: The council said each keeps their own thanks to themselves at the table.

li.label: thanks said at the table
li.description: I said the words before supper and the whole table heard them. It felt right to give thanks.

li.label: sat through the words
li.description: I had to sit and wait while somebody thanked their god for my supper. It went cold.

li.label: the words said at the shrine
li.description: I said the words at the god's place before supper. Not at the table, but they were said.

li.label: no thanks at the table
li.description: The council said nobody need give thanks at the table. We eat as though the food just came from nowhere.
